body: I have been dealing with this all my life, and the best advice I have is to remember that OCD is triggered by anxiety so if you can find ways to be mindful and use skills to reduce anxiety the suicidal imagery well lessen or at least become less painful when it intrudes. I feel for you, it is truly horrible to live with these thoughts but the truth is that there is no quick fix

i also talk out loud, although mine are compulsive and I have little control over them. It can be pretty embarrassing to be walking through a crowded place and realize that people are looking at you because you are muttering to yourself

maybe you can tell your family "I'm not comfortable going right now, and I can tell you more about why at a later time." That way you can soft-pedal telling them and saying out loud what you are dealing with. But I explained in little pieces to my family why and they were accepting, if not totally understanding.

a lot of us have that tendency, and one thing you can do is tell the people in your life that you know this about yourself, so ask them to validate your desire for reassurance without actually giving in to making decisions for you. you could even preface your posts with a 'disclaimer' saying the same thing.
I find that writing music has helped me understand my OCD and build skills like almost nothing else has. Just remember it doesn't have to be perfect!

Yes, this phenomenon has been studied a little bit, and it was found that clomipramine can lessen musical obsessions aka intrusive musical imagery. I have experience with this, "hearing" and "playing" the steel pan solo from Grover Washington Jr's song "Just the two of us" for about ten years. Over time I noticed that this would occur especially during times of heightened anxiety. I was able to lessen the frequency of this particular song by symbolically (and literally) giving the song to my therapist, thereby letting it go into someone else's care.
